title: 1976 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Ann and Barbara were comparing their ages and found that Barbara is as old as Ann was when Barbara was as old as Ann had been when Barbara was half as old as Ann is. If the sum of their present ages is \(44\) years, then Ann’s age is

solutions.text:
Let Ann’s and Barbara’s present ages be \(x\) and \(y,\) and let their constant age difference be \(d=x-y.\) At the first referenced time Ann was \(y,\) so Barbara was \(y-d.\) At the earlier referenced time Ann was that age \(y-d,\) so Barbara was \(y-2d.\) The final clause says this last age was \(\frac{x}{2}.\) Hence \[ y-2(x-y)=\frac{x}{2}, \] which gives \(6y=5x.\) Together with \(x+y=44,\) this yields \(x=24\) and \(y=20.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let Ann’s and Barbara’s present ages be \(x\) and \(y,\) with \(x+y=44\)
Translate each “when” by subtracting the same elapsed time from both ages
